items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Allen Reuss as an example of a musician used in sessions when Benny Goodman was in town, but Jo Jones does not respond with any personal interaction or relationship.

ctx.x: trying to get a point across to the American public and to the world in general of what we were trying to do. We came from all left field. You had different kind of peoples came in just to be on the recording session, just to do something for posterity.

Hey, Jo, I might be able to answer that question in a little bit. At that time, Bill, as Jo said, 1937, I was in the Cotton Club with Cab. I came for the first time in 1936 and Jo was with Basie, they came into town in 1936. John Kirby's band was in town. Duke Ellington was around sometime between '36 and '37. The way that orchestras were picked for the band, Teddy Wilson had been picked as the leader, as you see by the first date that you did, right, Jo? Teddy Wilson had been picked as the leader. He was used as…

the thing, on the strength of the recommendation that Jo and Cozy, as being a pretty good guy in the bass section, they would use me. Now if Basie was in town they would use Jo Jones and Walter Page. If John Kirby's band happened to be in town at that time, and John Kirby certainly had seniority over me at that particular time, then John Kirby would be the bass player. So this is why the discography reads with all these different guys.
